claims: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of Ramadan’s month-long dawn-to-sunset fasting.
Eid al-Fitr is celebrated on the first three days of Shawwal.
Shawwal is the 10th month.
Eid al-Fitr is the "Festival of Breaking the Fast".
Eid al-Fitr falls on the first day of Shawwal.
Eid al-Fitr is based on the lunar calendar.
The Gregorian date of Eid al-Fitr shifts approximately 11 days earlier each year.
Muslims start Eid al-Fitr by attending special congregational prayers in mosques or open areas.
Muslims often take a different route home after Eid al-Fitr prayers.
Muslims pay Zakat al-Fitr before the Eid al-Fitr prayer.
Zakat al-Fitr is charity for the needy.
Friends and family exchange greetings of "Eid Mubarak" (Blessed Eid) or "Eid Said" (Happy Eid) on Eid al-Fitr.
People wear new or best clothes on Eid al-Fitr.
People decorate homes on Eid al-Fitr.
People gather with family for large, often sweet-heavy, meals on Eid al-Fitr.
Children receive "Eidi" (money or gifts) on Eid al-Fitr.
Eid al-Fitr is "Lesser Eid".
Eid al-Adha is "Greater Eid".
Eid al-Adha occurs later in the year than Eid al-Fitr.
Eid al-Adha commemorates Prophet Ibrahim's sacrifice.
